chapter: Learning drums, WPA band and dance halls
title: Playing the Buckhorn dance hall and taking Van Gaiman's place
summary: Sal says everyone played the dance hall on Burgundy Street and tells how he got the drum job there from Van Gaiman.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, sure. The bass shot, man. It was us. Uh, Secretary of Interior. Uh-huh. Harry Lickish, you know. Oh, yeah. And the guy who had the, uh, the N.O. Ray, uh, Holly Johnson. Well, I mean, I'm kind of a historian myself, you know. Yeah, you know. Besides the music, you know. The foot. Pardon? You talk about, oh, yeah, this is what I want to mention, but it was to you. Uh-huh. I don't think hardly anybody has ever mentioned the foot and dance hall. Not yet, yeah. Which, every musician in town played at the foot and dance hall, you know. Everybody. Uh-huh. Well, I played there when it was called the Buckhorn on Burgundy Street. Uh-huh. One-twenty-five Burgundy.

The Buckhorn? The Buckhorn. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. The chief was a long chief of police and Captain Harry Drexel. I played in there. I took Van Gaiman's place. The only two drummers played in there was Van Gaiman and me. I took Van's place. As a matter of fact, how they came about. I said, I want to get to you straight. You can't do somebody else. It's difficult, but I'm telling you it's the real truth. Van was a fine drummer. I used to go play for Van Gaiman. One time there, Steve Lloyd Kean, a good promoter. He got the best job in town. He was a slipper. He was a slipper. He'd slip up to a fine band. He tried about two or three drummers and he couldn't cut the mustard. There was a reason. So I told Steve, I said, we were on the New St. Neville, right next door Steve's house on Kamp Street. I said, Steve, I'm going to go find a fine drummer. He said, yeah, but you got to read. I said, this guy could read anything. I used to go by the South Spine and I played together snare drum and did the music up there. I knew what he could do. He said, where's he playing? He laughed and I said, man, the four and the answer are all, man. I think at that time they had a, I forget, Shawy already left, see, with Tony Amarillo's playing trumpet. And he came over there and heard Van play. So then he brought him to Rehorsen. So I was very interested in how he made out, see, I noticed he make it, see. Steve, how he make out. He's fine, man. I hate it, see. So Van said to me, man, give me his job before, see. I had the job before, Van, with Steve, see. I told him, oh, Van, have you ever met Van Dam? Oh, yeah. He's a nice fellow. And Van said, hey, Van, I'm young and he, Van, see. I said, you want a good job? He's wondering why I didn't take it, see. Well, I got a job. Why don't you take it? He says, I'm not good enough. I said, I can't really good enough. Can you give me the job? He said, yeah. So I got the job from Steve, see. So I went to the front. So for about a week, all the drums come up and I want to play the drum. He said, ah, Monk was just beginning to learn how to play the peck on, you know, Monk, you know. I said, go on, man, play some drums for Monk. Oh, man, I want to play the drum, man, see. I want to play the peck on, see. And they said, learn it. And what else? He played the peck on, see. And so after that, everybody said, where's Van? Oh, he's taking a few nights off, you know. My job is over at my job, see. So Van said, I can't keep this up, you know. The guy's going to play for him, sit in for him, man, Leo. Leo's playing with Abbey Brunner at the halfway house, see. But he's going to play for me for kicks, you know. Leo, Ray, Purdue. I'll tell you another good drum. Remember Rod? You ever hear of him, Rod? I'm never. No, no, I didn't know him.
I knew Buck is the one.
